dialogues.speaker: Kayabuki Ikkei
dialogues.text: "Outlander Brigade," the latest trailblazer in Inazuman light literature, has just made its debut. Wanna have a look?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Outlander Brigade"?

dialogues.speaker: Kayabuki Ikkei
dialogues.text: That's right! Striking name, eh? Don't worry, the text itself reads just as well as it sounds like it might!

dialogues.speaker: Kayabuki Ikkei
dialogues.text: Trust me, this series is going to be a big hit for sure!

dialogues.speaker: Kayabuki Ikkei
dialogues.text: At the moment, "When the Wind of Death Blew Towards the Blond Samurai" is just the first volume in the series. As for the second and third volumes, I already have some ideas for their names...

dialogues.speaker: Kayabuki Ikkei
dialogues.text: The second shall be named "The Fatal Flowery Blade," and the third, "Blond Samurai, Go With the Wind."

dialogues.speaker: Kayabuki Ikkei
dialogues.text: Heh, I guess you could call me a prodigious talent in naming things.

dialogues.speaker: Kayabuki Ikkei
dialogues.text: That said, I haven't decided on what to write exactly... although that's not really important at the moment.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How are sales?

dialogues.speaker: Kayabuki Ikkei
dialogues.text: None at the moment.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not a single one?

dialogues.speaker: Kayabuki Ikkei
dialogues.text: Well... yes.

dialogues.speaker: Kayabuki Ikkei
dialogues.text: That said, I believe that this state is only temporary. I mean, even the most famous authors were unknown once.

dialogues.speaker: Kayabuki Ikkei
dialogues.text: Such dilemmas are just like the martial training written about in the books — a test of one's heart and character. As such, I must persevere...

dialogues.speaker: Kayabuki Ikkei
dialogues.text: One day, my works will be acknowledged by the world at large!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you.

dialogues.speaker: Kayabuki Ikkei
dialogues.text: See you around!

dialogues.speaker: Kayabuki Ikkei
dialogues.text: Wait a moment — you're not going to buy a copy after all that?

dialogues.speaker: Kayabuki Ikkei
dialogues.text: Hey, how's it going?

choices.text: About the novel you want to write...

response.speaker: Kayabuki Ikkei
response.text: I grew up reading storybooks and novels, and back then, I dreamed of becoming like Iwakura or Kitain, an unparalleled warrior and slayer of demons.

response.speaker: Kayabuki Ikkei
response.text: I only realized that I lacked that talent after I'd grown up. That's why I decided to write stories about warriors instead. The art of making lines of words shine is a martial art in and of itself, wouldn't you say?

response.speaker: Kayabuki Ikkei
response.text: I mean, I could've still have chosen to become an attaché to some military officer, but I must say that I'd prefer penning the tale of a carefree outland warrior like yourself.

response.speaker: Kayabuki Ikkei
response.text: I'm very much looking forward to your performance — just as much as I'd love to write it down, haha!

response.speaker: Kayabuki Ikkei
response.text: In the early days, this was a mysterious rite used by the Tengu-Kin as a means of making a ruckus.

response.speaker: Kayabuki Ikkei
response.text: Even after they were banned, people would still sometimes organize it in secret. The organizers' identities are still shrouded in mystery.

response.speaker: Kayabuki Ikkei
response.text: It's a rather rowdy brawl, all things considered. Anyone can participate, mortal or monster.

response.speaker: Kayabuki Ikkei
response.text: That's got to be a dream come true for those who long for battle, eh?
